title: Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship 2026: CAD $4,000 Stipend and Reporting Support for Journalists in Global South Countries
summary: The Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship 2026 is now accepting applications from journalists in ODA-recipient countries who are interested in producing powerful, fact-based journalism about local solutions to global crises, with a particular focus on gender . Launched by the Equality Fund in partnership with Canadian Journalists for Free Expression (CJFE) and African Women in Media (AWiM) , the inaugural fellowship is designed to support journalists who are reporting directly from the communities affected by major social, economic, environmental, political and human rights challenges. The programme will select up to five journalists for a fellowship running from January to September 2027 , providing a CAD $4,000 stipend , up to CAD $500 in reporting expenses , professional learning opportunities, safety training, expert-led online sessions and an in-person convening with travel expenses covered. For journalists looking for opportunities to strengthen their reporting, develop an important investigative or solutions-focused story, expand their professional networks and highlight community-led responses to global challenges, the fellowship provides a structured platform to undertake this work. About the Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship The inaugural Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship was created in response to the need for strong, independent and fact-based journalism at a time when communities around the world are experiencing interconnected crises. The programme is particularly interested in stories that move beyond simply documenting problems and instead explore local solutions to global crises . Its central focus is on identifying and amplifying initiatives, people and approaches within communities that are responding to challenges and creating meaningful change. The fellowship s core objective is for each journalist to produce and publish at least one story focused on local solutions to a global crisis, with gender serving as an important lens. The Equality Fund describes the fellowship as an opportunity to support journalists who are reporting from their own communities and whose work can help bring locally developed solutions into wider public view. What Does the Fellowship Focus On? The fellowship is not limited to one specific type of crisis. Applicants can explore a broad range of issues affecting communities around the world. Potential areas include: Climate change and environmental challenges Gender-based violence Authoritarianism Anti-rights movements Sexual and reproductive health and rights Economic injustice War and armed conflict Human rights Democracy and civic space Other interconnected global crises where communities are developing locally relevant responses. The emphasis, however, is not simply on reporting the existence of these crises. Fellows are expected to investigate and report on solutions emerging from within affected communities . This means a strong fellowship proposal could potentially examine how women, grassroots organisations, community leaders, activists, local institutions, first responders, farmers, entrepreneurs or other community actors are responding to major challenges. Key Objective of the Fellowship The central objective of the Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship is straightforward: each fellow should produce at least one published story about local solutions to global crises, with a focus on gender. The fellowship therefore combines financial support with professional development and editorial opportunities. Rather than functioning solely as a training programme, the fellowship is structured around the production of journalism. Successful applicants will have the opportunity to develop their proposed story while receiving support, mentorship, training and access to experts throughout the programme. The programme is scheduled to run from January through September 2027 , with six months of programming followed by an additional three months for fellows to finalise publication. What Does the Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship Offer? Successful fellows will receive a combination of financial, professional and networking support. 1. CAD $4,000 Fellowship Stipend Each selected journalist will receive a CAD $4,000 stipend . The stipend is intended to support fellows during their participation in the programme and enable them to dedicate time and resources to developing their journalism project. According to the official guidelines, freelance journalists who are already being paid a publication fee by their publishing outlet may retain that publication fee in addition to the fellowship stipend. Full-time staff journalists, meanwhile, will be required to notify their newsroom about the fellowship stipend. 2. Up to CAD $500 for Reporting Expenses In addition to the stipend, fellows can receive up to CAD $500 in reporting expenses . This additional support can help facilitate the practical reporting process associated with developing and producing the fellowship story. For journalists reporting from their own communities, this may provide useful additional resources for gathering information, conducting interviews and carrying out field reporting connected to their proposed project. 3. Six Months of Fellowship Programming The core fellowship programming will run for approximately six months . The programme is scheduled to begin in January 2027 , followed by an additional three-month period during which fellows can finalise their publications. Overall, the fellowship programme and publication period will run through September 2027 . 4. Monthly Online Meetings Fellows will participate in monthly online meetings featuring journalists and experts. These sessions are designed to expose fellows to different areas of journalism practice, reporting, ethics, safety and coverage of complex global issues. The programme s listed contributors include: Nina Lakhani , a climate journalist associated with The Guardian and Drilled. Kelly Kimball , a journalism and ethics professor at the City University of New York. Professionals involved in journalist safety training from the International Women s Media Foundation (IWMF) . Experts associated with the Freedom of the Press Foundation . These sessions can provide fellows with opportunities to develop their professional knowledge while working on their fellowship projects. 5. Journalism Safety Training Safety is an important component of the fellowship. Selected journalists will receive safety-related training involving organisations working in the field of journalist protection, including the International Women s Media Foundation and Freedom of the Press Foundation . This is particularly relevant for journalists covering sensitive subjects such as conflict, human rights violations, gender-based violence, political repression or other challenging environments. 6. One In-Person Convening The fellowship will also include one in-person convening . The specific location and timing of the gathering have not yet been determined, but travel expenses will be covered . The convening will give fellows an opportunity to meet in person, build professional relationships and exchange experiences arising from their reporting work. Who Can Apply for the Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship? The fellowship is intended for working journalists in ODA-recipient countries . Importantly, applicants do not have to be employed full-time by a traditional newsroom. The programme is open to: Full-time journalists. Independent journalists. Freelance journalists. Journalists working across different media platforms. Journalists producing text-based reporting. Digital journalists. Video journalists. Audio journalists. The fellowship specifically encourages journalists to report on their own communities and geographies . Minimum Eligibility Requirements The official 2026 application guidelines provide additional requirements that applicants should carefully review before applying. Applicants must have at least three years of journalism experience. Candidates are required to demonstrate a minimum of three years of journalism experience . Applicants should therefore be able to show a sustained track record of journalistic work rather than relying solely on academic qualifications or an interest in journalism. Applicants must be located in an ODA-recipient country Applicants should be located in an ODA-recipient country and should be reporting on communities in those countries. The fellowship uses the OECD framework for determining ODA-recipient countries. Applicants must provide three journalism samples. Candidates are required to submit three strong journalism samples demonstrating a range of relevant work. Applicants should therefore select portfolio pieces that best demonstrate their reporting ability, storytelling skills, editorial judgement and experience covering issues relevant to the fellowship. English proficiency is required. The official application guidelines state that applicants must be fluent in English , which is the Equality Fund s working language. Applicants must be able to participate in meetings in Eastern Standard Time. Because the fellowship includes online programming, applicants must be able to accommodate meetings taking place during daytime hours in Eastern Standard Time . Prospective applicants should therefore consider the time-zone difference between their location and Eastern Standard Time before applying. Applicants need a bank account capable of receiving international transfers. Applicants should have access to a bank account capable of accepting international Electronic Wire Transfers . This requirement is important because the fellowship includes financial support. Gender and Diversity Eligibility The fellowship is designed to be inclusive. The original fellowship announcement states that applications are welcomed from: Women Men LGBTQI+ people The detailed application guidelines further state that women, non-binary and trans people are encouraged to apply . The guidelines also reference the Equality Fund s values around equality and diversity across areas including race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, national origin and disability. This means applicants do not need to belong to one particular gender category to be considered. Eligible Countries and Regions The Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship is open to journalists based in ODA-recipient countries . The opportunity therefore has a broad geographical scope covering eligible countries across the Global South rather than being restricted to one particular region. Applicants should verify that their country appears on the relevant OECD DAC list of ODA recipients before submitting an application. For African journalists, this makes the fellowship particularly relevant to journalists working in eligible African countries, while the programme also extends to eligible countries in other parts of the Global South. What Kind of Story Should Applicants Propose? One of the most important aspects of the fellowship is the proposed journalism story. The programme is looking for reporting that explores local solutions to global crises , particularly through a gender-focused perspective. Applicants should therefore think beyond simply identifying a problem. A strong concept could explore questions such as What major crisis is affecting the community? How is the crisis affecting women or other groups differently? What local individuals, organisations or communities are responding? What practical solution has emerged? What evidence exists that the approach is working or producing meaningful results? What barriers are limiting the solution? What lessons could other communities learn from the experience? Potential stories could focus on women farmers developing responses to climate-related challenges, community-led responses to gender-based violence, local approaches to economic injustice, grassroots responses to conflict or initiatives protecting human rights. The programme s emphasis on local solutions means applicants should demonstrate a clear connection between the proposed story and the community in which they work. Editorial Independence An important feature of the fellowship is that fellows will retain complete editorial independence . This means journalists remain responsible for their journalistic work and editorial decisions. The official guidelines also state that fellows retain intellectual property rights over their work , while the Equality Fund retains the right to publish or reproduce the work for purposes of promoting the fellowship. This distinction is important for journalists who are concerned about ownership and editorial control when participating in externally funded journalism programmes. Editorial Commitment From a News Outlet The fellowship uses a phased application process. Shortlisted applicants will be asked to provide a letter of editorial commitment from a news outlet . This demonstrates that there is an intended publication pathway for the proposed journalism. For applicants who are self-publishing, the guidelines indicate that the editorial commitment may, in some cases, be replaced by a fact-checking plan . Applicants should therefore think carefully about how their proposed story will ultimately reach an audience. AI Use in the Application and Journalism Process Applicants should pay particular attention to the fellowship s rules concerning artificial intelligence. According to the official fellowship announcement: AI use is not permitted in the proposal and application. AI use during the journalistic process must be disclosed to the programme . Such use must be approved in advance . This is an important requirement for applicants preparing their submissions and developing their fellowship stories. Applicants should read the official guidelines carefully and follow the programme s requirements rather than assuming that general AI policies from other journalism organisations apply. Additional Expectations for Fellows Beyond producing a story, fellows should be prepared to follow responsible journalism practices. The application guidelines state that fellows should be willing to: Follow trauma-informed reporting best practices . Conduct community roundtables where possible . Maintain editorial independence. Work collaboratively with the fellowship community. Participate in the programme s online meetings and learning activities. These expectations reflect the fellowship s focus on reporting complex issues involving communities that may be experiencing significant social, political, economic or humanitarian pressures. Fellowship Timeline The Equality Fund expects the programme to follow this general timeline: Stage Timeline Application period 2026 Application deadline November 8, 2026 Fellowship begins January 2027 Core programming Six months Publication finalisation period Additional three months Programme period January–September 2027 Fellows selected Up to 5 journalists The official application guidelines specify that applications close on November 8, 2026 at midnight Eastern Standard Time . What Applicants Should Prepare Before applying, prospective candidates should prepare the required materials and information. A useful application preparation checklist includes: Confirm country eligibility Verify that your country is included among ODA-recipient countries. Document your journalism experience Ensure you can demonstrate at least three years of relevant journalism experience. Select three strong journalism samples Choose work that demonstrates your reporting range and ability to cover relevant issues. Develop a clear story concept Identify a compelling local solution to a global crisis and explain how gender is connected to the story. Identify the community you will report on The fellowship expects journalists to report on their own communities and geographies. Consider your publication pathway If you work with a news organisation, consider how you can secure an editorial commitment. Freelancers and self-publishing journalists should review the alternative requirements carefully. Review the AI rules Applicants should understand the restrictions on AI use in the application and the disclosure and approval requirements for AI use during the journalistic process. Check your availability Make sure you can participate in online meetings during the required Eastern Standard Time hours. Confirm your banking arrangements Ensure your bank can receive international electronic wire transfers. Review the official application guidelines Applicants should read the full guidelines before submitting their application. Why This Fellowship Is Relevant to Journalists in the Global South The fellowship is specifically designed around journalists reporting from communities in ODA-recipient countries. That local perspective is central to the programme. Instead of relying exclusively on international correspondents or external observers, the fellowship seeks to support journalists who already understand the communities they are covering. This can be particularly important when reporting on subjects such as gender inequality, climate change, economic injustice, conflict, human rights and gender-based violence, where local knowledge and relationships can provide important context. The programme s focus on solutions journalism also provides an opportunity to investigate how communities are responding to difficult circumstances rather than focusing exclusively on the challenges themselves. About the Fellowship Partners The Equality Fund is implementing the journalism fellowship in partnership with two organisations with experience in journalism and media advocacy. Canadian Journalists for Free Expression The Equality Fund has partnered with Canadian Journalists for Free Expression (CJFE) , an organisation focused on supporting freedom of expression and journalism. The partnership brings an additional journalism and press-freedom dimension to the fellowship. African Women in Media The fellowship also partners with African Women in Media (AWiM) . AWiM s involvement is particularly relevant to the programme s focus on gender equality, journalism and media systems across Africa and beyond. Fellowship Financial and Professional Benefits at a Glance Successful applicants can expect: CAD $4,000 stipend Up to CAD $500 for reporting expenses Six months of structured programming Three additional months to finalise publication Monthly online meetings Access to experienced journalists and experts Journalism and ethics learning Journalist safety training One in-person convening Travel expenses for the in-person convening Editorial independence Retention of intellectual property rights over fellows work, subject to the Equality Fund s stated publication/reproduction rights Opportunity to produce and publish at least one major story focused on local solutions to global crises and gender. Application Deadline The deadline for the Equality Fund Global Journalism Fellowship 2026 is November 8, 2026, at midnight Eastern Standard Time . The official application guidelines also describe the closing time as 11 p.m. Eastern Standard Time in the application instructions, so applicants should submit well before the final day to avoid any time-zone or technical issues. Because the programme is competitive and requires several supporting elements, including journalism samples and potentially an editorial commitment, applicants are encouraged to begin preparing their submissions early. APPLY HERE How to Apply for the Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship Interested journalists should review the official application guidelines and submit their applications through the Equality Fund s designated application process. Applicants should carefully review all eligibility requirements, documentation requirements, editorial expectations and AI-related rules before submitting their application. Visit HERE for more information about the Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship 2026. Conclusion The Equality Fund Journalism Fellowship 2026 provides an opportunity for experienced journalists in ODA-recipient countries to receive financial support, professional development, safety training and networking opportunities while producing journalism focused on local solutions to global crises through a gender lens . The programme is open to journalists working across text, digital, video and audio platforms, including both full-time and independent freelance journalists. Successful fellows will receive a CAD $4,000 stipend , up to CAD $500 in reporting expenses , access to monthly expert-led sessions, safety training and an in-person convening with travel expenses covered. Applicants should pay particular attention to the additional requirements: a minimum of three years of journalism experience , three strong journalism samples, English fluency, availability for meetings in Eastern Standard Time and the ability to receive international electronic wire transfers. The programme also places strong emphasis on reporting from journalists own communities and maintaining editorial independence. With applications closing on November 8, 2026 , eligible journalists who have a strong story idea about a locally driven response to a major global challenge can review the official guidelines and prepare their application for consideration for the 2027 fellowship cohort. title: Sutton Trust 2026 Programmes: Free Access Apprenticeships and Pathways to the Professions for UK Students
summary: The Sutton Trust has opened applications for two major programmes designed to help young people from less advantaged backgrounds explore university, degree apprenticeships and professional careers. The Access Apprenticeships and Pathways to the Professions programmes provide students with practical guidance, exposure to leading career sectors and opportunities to build confidence as they prepare for their next steps after school or college. Unlike many career-development opportunities that require participants to cover participation costs, Sutton Trust programmes are completely free to attend . According to the organisation, costs including travel, accommodation, food and activities are covered by the Sutton Trust and its university and employer partners. For students considering competitive professional careers or degree apprenticeships, these programmes can provide an opportunity to gain a better understanding of different career routes while receiving practical advice about future education and employment decisions. About the Sutton Trust The Sutton Trust is an organisation focused on improving social mobility and access to educational and career opportunities for young people from less advantaged backgrounds. Through partnerships with universities, employers, schools and other organisations, the Sutton Trust runs programmes intended to help students make informed decisions about their futures and improve their access to leading universities and careers. Its programmes cover areas including: Higher education Schools and colleges Apprenticeships Access to professional careers Career exploration Educational progression Social mobility The organisation states that its programmes are designed to give young people practical advice, inspiration and greater confidence about their future. For 2026, two opportunities currently open for applications are Access Apprenticeships and Pathways to the Professions . 1. Sutton Trust Access Apprenticeships 2026 The Access Apprenticeships programme is designed for students who want to understand more about degree apprenticeships and the opportunities available through this alternative route into higher education and professional employment. Degree apprenticeships combine elements of university-level study with workplace experience. This means that students can gain academic qualifications while developing practical experience in an employment environment. For students who are uncertain about whether the traditional university route is the right option for them, learning about degree apprenticeships can help them understand the range of pathways available after completing school or college. Applications Are Now Open Applications for the 2026 Access Apprenticeships programme opened on: 1 September 2026 The stated closing period is: November 2026 The information provided does not specify one exact closing day in November, so prospective applicants should check the official Sutton Trust programme page for the precise deadline applicable to the programme. Where Is Access Apprenticeships Held? The programme is offered in: London Manchester Students selected for the programme therefore have the opportunity to participate in activities connected with these locations. Who Can Apply for Access Apprenticeships? The programme is intended for students at the following educational levels: Year 12 in England Year 12 in Wales Year 13 in Northern Ireland S5 in Scotland The programme is particularly focused on young people from less advantaged backgrounds , consistent with the Sutton Trust s broader social mobility mission. Applicants should therefore carefully review the detailed eligibility requirements on the official programme page before applying, as the information provided here gives the core educational-year requirements but does not reproduce every possible eligibility criterion. What Can Students Gain from Access Apprenticeships? One of the central purposes of Access Apprenticeships is to help students understand how degree apprenticeships work and what they can offer. Participants can gain greater awareness of: Understanding Degree Apprenticeships Students can learn how degree apprenticeships differ from conventional university programmes and how academic study can be combined with employment. This can help participants understand the structure of apprenticeship-based higher education and whether this route aligns with their interests and career goals. Exploring Career Opportunities The programme can introduce students to career possibilities that may be available through degree apprenticeships. Rather than simply focusing on academic qualifications, participants can gain insight into how education, employment and professional development can be connected. Building Confidence Choosing a career pathway can be challenging, particularly for students who may not have extensive access to professional networks or career guidance. The Sutton Trust s programmes are designed to provide practical advice and help students feel more confident about their future decisions. Exposure to Employers and Professional Environments Because Sutton Trust programmes are delivered in partnership with universities and employers, participants can gain exposure to organisations and professional environments that may otherwise be difficult to access. Understanding Alternative Routes into Professional Careers Degree apprenticeships can provide an alternative pathway into higher education and employment. By learning about this option at an early stage, students can make more informed decisions when considering what to do after school or college. 2. Sutton Trust Pathways to the Professions 2026 The second opportunity currently open for applications is Pathways to the Professions . This programme is designed to introduce students to a range of professional careers and provide practical information about what it takes to enter different sectors. The programme covers several highly competitive professional fields, including: Banking and Finance Engineering Law Medicine Veterinary Medicine This makes the programme particularly relevant to students who already have an interest in one of these areas or who are still exploring which professional pathway they would like to pursue. Applications Are Now Open Applications opened on: 1 September 2026 The closing dates vary depending on the specific programme. The Sutton Trust states that applications close at different points across: October and November 2026 Students should therefore check the individual Pathways to the Professions programme they are interested in because the precise deadline may differ according to the career pathway and programme location. Where Is Pathways to the Professions Available? The programme is described as being available through: National programmes Regional programmes Online programmes In-person programmes This gives students different ways of participating depending on the specific pathway and programme being offered. The availability of online opportunities can also make it possible for students to participate without necessarily travelling to a central location, although students should check the format of the specific programme they wish to apply for. Professional Fields Covered by Pathways to the Professions Banking and Finance Students interested in financial services can use the programme to learn more about careers in banking and finance. The sector encompasses a wide range of roles, including financial analysis, investment, banking, accounting, economics, risk management and related professional areas. Exposure to the sector at school level can help students understand the qualifications, skills and career pathways associated with financial services. Engineering Engineering is another professional area covered by the programme. Students can explore the broad range of opportunities available within engineering and gain a better understanding of the relationship between science, mathematics, technology and professional practice. The programme can be particularly useful for students who are considering technical or STEM-related careers but want greater insight into what professional engineering careers involve. Law For students considering a career in law, the programme provides an opportunity to learn more about the profession and the pathway towards becoming a legal professional. Students can use such exposure to develop a better understanding of the legal profession and the academic and professional preparation it requires. Medicine Medicine is another major professional pathway covered by the Sutton Trust programme. Students interested in becoming doctors can gain exposure to the profession and receive information that can help them understand the pathway towards a medical career. This type of early career guidance can be particularly valuable because medicine typically involves a lengthy and highly structured educational and professional pathway. Veterinary Medicine Students interested in working with animals and pursuing veterinary careers can also explore veterinary medicine through the programme. The opportunity can help students gain greater awareness of the profession and consider whether the field aligns with their academic interests and long-term career aspirations. What Makes the Sutton Trust Programmes Different? A major feature of both opportunities is their focus on access and social mobility . The Sutton Trust works to support young people who may face greater barriers to accessing leading universities and professional careers. The programmes are therefore not simply designed to provide career information. They are intended to connect students with practical guidance, institutions, employers and experiences that can help them better understand opportunities that may otherwise be unfamiliar. The Programmes Are Completely Free One of the most important benefits for applicants is that the Sutton Trust states that its programmes are free to attend . The Trust and its partners cover costs including: Travel Accommodation Food Activities This can reduce financial barriers that might otherwise prevent students from participating in educational and career-development programmes. For students and families concerned about the cost of attending external programmes, this is an important feature to consider. Universities and Employers Play an Important Role The Sutton Trust does not operate these programmes in isolation. The organisation works in partnership with universities and employers to provide students with practical information and experiences. This partnership model can give participants exposure to both sides of the education-to-employment pathway. Students can learn about: What it is like to study at university. What professional careers involve. The qualifications required for particular professions. Different routes into employment. The skills employers value. How to prepare for future education and career opportunities. This combination of educational and professional exposure can help students develop a broader understanding of the choices available to them. Key Benefits of the Sutton Trust 2026 Programmes Students selected for these programmes can benefit from several forms of support and exposure. 1. Free Participation The programmes do not charge students to attend, with the Sutton Trust and partners covering key participation costs. 2. Career Exploration Participants can explore professional careers before making major decisions about university courses, apprenticeships and employment. 3. Practical Advice The programmes focus on practical guidance rather than solely theoretical information. 4. University and Employer Exposure Participants can gain insight into both higher education and professional environments. 5. Greater Career Awareness Students can develop a clearer understanding of what different professional careers involve. 6. Confidence Building The programmes are intended to leave students feeling more informed, inspired and confident about their future. 7. Understanding Degree Apprenticeships Access Apprenticeships provides students with an opportunity to explore degree apprenticeships as a route combining employment and higher education. 8. Access to Professional Pathways Pathways to the Professions allows students to explore careers in areas such as finance, engineering, law, medicine and veterinary medicine. 9. National, Regional and Online Opportunities Pathways to the Professions includes different participation formats, with national, regional, online and in-person opportunities available depending on the programme. 10. Reduced Financial Barriers Because programme-related costs are covered, students may be able to participate without the financial burden associated with many external educational opportunities. Who Is Eligible to Apply? The Sutton Trust programmes described here are primarily aimed at young people studying in the UK who meet the specified school-year requirements. The stated age/education requirements are: Programme Eligible school year Location Access Apprenticeships Year 12 in England and Wales; Year 13 in Northern Ireland; S5 in Scotland London and Manchester Pathways to the Professions Year 12 in England and Wales; Year 13 in Northern Ireland; S5 in Scotland National and regional; online and in-person Applicants should also note the Sutton Trust s emphasis on supporting young people from less advantaged backgrounds . Because individual programmes may have additional requirements, prospective applicants should review the specific programme information before submitting an application. Countries and Regions Eligible The information provided does not present this as a worldwide scholarship or international fellowship. Instead, eligibility is structured around students attending school or college in the United Kingdom: England Wales Scotland Northern Ireland The educational-year terminology used by the Sutton Trust reflects the different education systems within the UK. For example: Year 12 applies to England and Wales. Year 13 applies to Northern Ireland. S5 applies to Scotland. Students outside these education systems should not assume that they qualify solely because they meet a similar age requirement. Is There a Race or Ethnicity Requirement? No specific race or ethnicity requirement is stated in the information provided. The programmes are instead described as supporting young people from less advantaged backgrounds as part of the Sutton Trust s wider focus on social mobility and reducing barriers to education and career opportunities. Applicants should therefore focus on the official eligibility criteria for the specific programme rather than assuming that eligibility is determined by race or ethnicity. Application Timeline for 2026 Students interested in applying should take note of the following dates. Access Apprenticeships Applications opened: 1 September 2026 Closing period: November 2026 Location: London and Manchester Pathways to the Professions Applications opened: 1 September 2026 Closing period: October and November 2026 Location: National and regional Format: In-person and online opportunities are available. Because Pathways to the Professions has different closing dates, applicants should check the specific programme they wish to join rather than relying on a single general deadline. How to Prepare for an Application Students interested in applying can take several practical steps before submitting their applications. 1. Identify Your Career Interests Think about the professional areas that interest you. For Pathways to the Professions, this could include: Banking and finance Engineering Law Medicine Veterinary medicine For students who are unsure about their career direction, the programmes can also serve as an opportunity to explore potential options. 2. Check Your School Year Confirm that you fall within the relevant education level: Year 12 in England and Wales Year 13 in Northern Ireland S5 in Scotland 3. Review the Specific Programme Do not rely only on general information about the Sutton Trust. Individual programmes may have their own requirements, application questions or deadlines. 4. Prepare Your Application Carefully Where an application asks about your interests, ambitions or background, provide clear and honest information. Explain why the programme interests you and what you hope to learn from the experience. 5. Apply Before the Deadline Because some Pathways to the Professions programmes have different closing dates, applicants should avoid waiting until the final day. Checking the individual programme deadline early can help prevent missing an opportunity because of a different closing date. Why Career Exposure Matters at School Level Career decisions can have long-term consequences, yet students do not always have equal access to information about professional pathways. A student whose family has extensive experience of a particular profession may already know about university requirements, professional qualifications, internships, degree apprenticeships and recruitment processes. Other students may have limited exposure to such information. Programmes such as those offered by the Sutton Trust are designed to help address this information gap by giving students access to practical guidance and exposure to universities and employers. Early exposure can help students: Identify careers they may not previously have considered. Understand what qualifications different professions require. Learn about university and apprenticeship routes. Develop greater confidence when planning their future. Ask informed questions about careers and education. Become more aware of opportunities available to them. Access Apprenticeships vs. Pathways to the Professions Although both programmes are operated by the Sutton Trust and share a focus on supporting young people from less advantaged backgrounds, they have different areas of emphasis. Access Apprenticeships This programme focuses specifically on degree apprenticeships . It is particularly relevant to students who want to explore a pathway that combines higher education with employment. The programme is offered in London and Manchester . Pathways to the Professions This programme focuses on exploring specific professional careers. The areas listed include: Banking and finance Engineering Law Medicine Veterinary medicine It offers national and regional opportunities , with both online and in-person programmes available. Students should therefore select the programme that most closely matches their educational and career interests. APPLY HERE Important Information for Applicants Before applying, prospective participants should remember the following: Applications opened on 1 September 2026 . Access Apprenticeships closes in November 2026 . Pathways to the Professions has deadlines spread across October and November 2026 . Access Apprenticeships is based in London and Manchester . Pathways to the Professions offers national and regional opportunities . Pathways to the Professions includes online and in-person opportunities . Applicants should be in Year 12 in England and Wales, Year 13 in Northern Ireland, or S5 in Scotland . The programmes are aimed at young people from less advantaged backgrounds . The Sutton Trust states that participation is completely free . Travel, accommodation, food and activities are covered by the Sutton Trust and its partners. Individual programmes may have additional eligibility requirements, so applicants should check the specific programme details before applying. Visit HERE for more information about the Sutton Trust 2026 Programmes. Conclusion The Sutton Trust s 2026 Access Apprenticeships and Pathways to the Professions programmes provide UK students from less advantaged backgrounds with opportunities to explore higher education, degree apprenticeships and professional careers at an important stage of their education. Access Apprenticeships is particularly relevant to students interested in understanding degree apprenticeships and the combination of university-level study with employment , while Pathways to the Professions gives students the opportunity to explore careers in banking and finance, engineering, law, medicine and veterinary medicine . The programmes are also notable for being free to attend , with the Sutton Trust and its partners covering costs such as travel, accommodation, food and activities. This can help reduce financial barriers and allow eligible students to participate in career and educational experiences that might otherwise be difficult to access. Students who meet the relevant school-year requirements and are interested in exploring their future education or career options should review the individual programme requirements and deadlines carefully. With applications opening from 1 September 2026 and closing between October and November 2026 , prospective applicants should begin preparing early and check the specific deadline for the programme they wish to pursue. The official Sutton Trust programme information should be consulted for the latest eligibility requirements, individual programme dates and application instructions. title: Become a Young European Ambassador: Join the YEA Network and Connect Youth Across Europe and the Eastern Neighbourhood
summary: The Young European Ambassadors (YEA) initiative is a youth network that brings together young people from the European Union and the Eastern Partnership countries to promote youth participation, awareness, dialogue, solidarity, and connections across borders. The initiative is part of the work of EU NEIGHBOURS east , which provides news, information and opportunities relating to the European Union s cooperation with its Eastern partners: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine . For young people interested in European affairs, youth engagement, community initiatives, democracy, human rights, environmental issues, gender equality, international cooperation and cross-border networking, the Young European Ambassadors initiative provides an opportunity to become part of a growing regional community. The network is celebrating its 10th anniversary in 2026 , marking a decade of youth-led activities, connections, campaigns, community initiatives and cooperation. What Is the Young European Ambassadors Initiative? The Young European Ambassadors initiative is a network that gives young people a platform to become active in their communities while connecting with peers across the Eastern Neighbourhood and the European Union. Since its launch, YEAs have worked to raise awareness about the EU s partnership with its Eastern neighbours, promote shared values and communicate opportunities available to young people. The initiative has also supported youth-led activities addressing issues such as: Democracy and civic participation Human rights Environmental protection Gender equality Youth empowerment European integration and cooperation Community development Solidarity and social engagement Awareness of educational and professional opportunities Cross-border youth networking Rather than being limited to one particular type of activity, the YEA network provides a space where young people can develop connections and participate in initiatives that respond to issues affecting their communities and the wider region. title: Impact100 DC Fellowship 2026: Fully Funded Philanthropy Fellowship for Women Ages 21–39 in the Washington, DC Region
summary: The Impact100 DC Fellowship 2026 offers an opportunity for women between the ages of 21 and 39 who are interested in philanthropy and community impact but may not have the financial resources to become full members of Impact100 DC. The fellowship allows participants to experience collective giving firsthand , take part in the organization s grant review process, contribute to community activities, and develop their leadership and philanthropic skills. Fellows become full members from the beginning of the fellowship at no cost , allowing them to participate alongside other Impact100 DC members without having to pay the standard membership contribution. Applications for the fellowship are currently open, with applications due October 15, 2026 . What Is the Impact100 DC Fellowship? The Impact100 DC Fellowship is designed for women who want to learn about philanthropy through direct participation rather than simply observing from the sidelines. The program gives Fellows the opportunity to become actively involved in how philanthropic resources are distributed and how grants can contribute to positive change in the community. Through the fellowship, participants experience the process of collective giving and help shape how Impact100 DC grants affect the community. Rather than requiring Fellows to make the standard financial contribution associated with membership, the fellowship provides qualifying participants with full membership at no cost. This creates an opportunity for women who are interested in philanthropy but may not have the financial resources to join Impact100 DC through the regular membership route. Experience Collective Giving Firsthand One of the central features of the Impact100 DC Fellowship is the opportunity to experience collective giving directly. Collective giving involves people coming together to pool resources and participate collectively in decisions about how those resources are distributed through grants. For Fellows, this means gaining practical exposure to the grantmaking process and understanding how philanthropic decisions can influence organizations and communities. Fellows are not passive participants. They are expected to become involved in the organization s activities and contribute to the grant review process. Full Membership From Day One at No Cost A major feature of the fellowship is that Fellows become full members from the beginning of the fellowship at no cost . The program emphasizes that Fellows do not simply observe Impact100 DC s activities. Instead, they participate as members and contribute to the organization s work. Fellows are expected to: Serve on at least one grant review committee. Contribute their skills to outreach, events, or communications. Connect with Impact100 DC members. Attend events and member activities. Participate actively in the community. Develop their leadership experience through involvement in the organization. This structure allows Fellows to gain practical experience while also contributing their own skills and perspectives. Grant Review Committee Participation Participation in the grant review process is a required component of the fellowship. Each Fellow must serve on at least one grant review committee . This gives Fellows direct experience with an important aspect of philanthropy: reviewing grant opportunities and participating in the process through which philanthropic resources can support community organizations. For women interested in nonprofit organizations, social impact, community development, charitable giving, or philanthropy, this experience can provide an opportunity to better understand how grantmaking works in practice. Opportunities to Contribute Skills Fellows can also contribute their individual skills to areas such as: Outreach Events Communications This means the fellowship is not limited to grant review. Fellows can also become involved in activities that help build and maintain the Impact100 DC community. Participants can use their existing professional, academic, creative, organizational, communication, or community-building skills while gaining new experience through their involvement. Networking and Community Building Another component of the fellowship is the opportunity to connect with existing Impact100 DC members. Fellows are encouraged to: Connect with members. Attend organizational events. Participate in member activities. Build relationships within the Impact100 DC community. Develop their leadership abilities. This provides an environment in which Fellows can learn from other members while developing connections around philanthropy and community impact. Who Should Apply? The Impact100 DC Fellowship is intended for women who meet the program s geographic and age requirements and who are genuinely interested in participating in philanthropy. The program identifies several characteristics of women who should apply. 1. Women Living or Working in the Eligible Washington, DC Region Applicants must live or work in one of the locations specified by Impact100 DC. Eligible locations include: Washington, DC Montgomery County, Maryland Prince George s County, Maryland Arlington County, Virginia Fairfax County, Virginia City of Alexandria, Virginia City of Falls Church, Virginia City of Fairfax, Virginia 2. Applicants Between 21 and 39 Applicants must be between 21 and 39 years old . The fellowship is specifically designed for women in this age range who are interested in becoming more actively involved in philanthropy. 3. Interest in Philanthropy Applicants should have a passion for making an impact through philanthropy. The fellowship is particularly relevant to women who want to understand how collective giving can contribute to community change and who are interested in participating directly in philanthropic activities. 4. Willingness to Participate Actively The fellowship requires active participation. Applicants should be excited about participating in: Committees Events Member activities Grant review Community-building activities The program is therefore intended for participants who are prepared to contribute time, skills, ideas, and energy to the Impact100 DC community. Fellowship Funding and Membership Support The Impact100 DC Fellowship is made possible through financial support from the organization s existing members and other supporters. According to the program information, fellowships are funded through the generosity of members who contribute above the $1,000 membership level , as well as through donations from corporate sponsors and other Impact100 DC supporters. This support allows Fellows to participate as full members without paying the standard membership cost. What Fellows Can Gain Although the fellowship is primarily centered on participation in philanthropy and community giving, the program can provide several forms of practical experience. Practical Philanthropy Experience Fellows participate directly in the grant review process, providing firsthand exposure to philanthropic decision-making. Leadership Development By participating in committees, events, outreach, communications, and member activities, Fellows can develop leadership and organizational experience. Community Connections Participants have opportunities to connect with Impact100 DC members and become part of a wider philanthropic community. Understanding Grantmaking Serving on a grant review committee can help Fellows understand how grantmaking processes operate and how philanthropic resources can be directed toward community needs. Professional and Personal Growth The fellowship provides an environment in which participants can contribute their existing skills while developing new knowledge, relationships, and leadership experience. Impact100 DC Fellowship Application Timeline The fellowship follows a multi-stage annual application process. September: Applications Become Available Applications become available for the following fellowship year in September. October 15: Applications Due The application deadline is October 15, 2026 . December: Fellows Selected Fellows are expected to be selected by the end of December . January: Fellowship Begins The one-year fellowship begins in January . The fellowship can be renewed for a second year , providing selected participants with the possibility of continuing their involvement beyond the initial fellowship year. Fellowship Duration The initial fellowship lasts one year . The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity for sustained involvement in Impact100 DC rather than being limited to a short-term event or workshop. Fellows become full members from day one and are expected to participate actively in the organization s work, including serving on at least one grant review committee, contributing skills to outreach, events, or communications, attending activities, connecting with members, and developing as leaders. The fellowship begins in January , lasts one year, and can be renewed for a second year. Applications are due October 15, 2026 , making it important for interested applicants to review the eligibility requirements and prepare their applications ahead of the deadline. For women interested in philanthropy, collective giving, community engagement, and leadership development, the program provides a structured opportunity to gain practical experience while contributing to Impact100 DC s grantmaking and community activities. title: TradeRoots Africa 2026–2027: ICC Programme Helping African SMEs Become Export-Ready and Access Regional and Global Markets
summary: African small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) seeking to expand beyond their domestic markets can now apply for TradeRoots Africa , an initiative of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) Centre of Entrepreneurship designed to help businesses become export-ready and compete more effectively across African and international markets. The programme is particularly focused on helping African SMEs navigate the practical challenges associated with regional and international trade, including export compliance, trade documentation, market access, digital trade, logistics, customs, trade finance, mentorship and business development. Applications for TradeRoots Africa are currently open, with the application deadline set for 15 October 2026 . The programme is scheduled to officially launch in November 2026 and continue through August 2027 . What Is TradeRoots Africa? TradeRoots Africa is an SME-focused trade development programme established by the ICC Centre of Entrepreneurship to help African businesses translate regional and continental trade opportunities into practical business growth. The initiative was launched at the 2025 B20 Summit in South Africa and is designed around the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and the Regional Economic Communities (RECs) . Rather than focusing only on theoretical knowledge about international trade, TradeRoots Africa takes a practical approach. The programme aims to help participating businesses develop the knowledge, capabilities, connections and resources needed to move towards actual export activity. According to the ICC, African SMEs represent approximately 90% of businesses on the continent and employ around 70% of the workforce , yet fewer than 20% formally export. The programme therefore seeks to address some of the barriers preventing otherwise viable African businesses from accessing regional and international markets. Why TradeRoots Africa Was Created Expanding a business into another country can involve considerably more than simply finding international customers. African SMEs can face multiple interconnected barriers when attempting to enter regional and global markets. These include: High costs associated with international trade. Complex regulatory and customs requirements. Limited access to digital trade tools. Infrastructure constraints. Difficulty accessing appropriate financing. Limited knowledge of export procedures. Challenges understanding regional and international markets. Limited access to potential buyers and business networks. The ICC notes that these challenges are interconnected, meaning that addressing one obstacle in isolation may not be sufficient to turn an SME into a successful exporter. TradeRoots Africa therefore brings several forms of support together in a structured programme intended to take participating businesses from foundational trade knowledge towards export acceleration. The Six Key Pillars of TradeRoots Africa TradeRoots Africa is structured around six major areas of support. Together, these pillars are intended to provide participating SMEs with practical capabilities for regional and international trade. 1. Trade Knowledge and Market Access Businesses will receive support in understanding trade requirements and identifying opportunities to access markets beyond their domestic market. This pillar is particularly important for SMEs that may have a product or service with growth potential but lack sufficient knowledge of export procedures, market requirements and regional trade opportunities. 2. Trade Finance Access to finance can be an important factor in a company s ability to enter new markets. TradeRoots Africa incorporates trade finance into its support framework, helping businesses develop greater readiness around financing requirements associated with international trade. 3. Logistics, Customs and Air Transport Cross-border trade requires businesses to understand how goods move between markets and how customs and logistical processes affect exports. The programme therefore includes logistics, customs and air transport as one of its six central pillars. 4. Digital Trade Tools Digital technologies are increasingly important for businesses seeking customers and opportunities beyond their domestic markets. TradeRoots Africa includes digital trade tools among its core areas of support, with later programme activities also focusing on e-commerce and related digital capabilities. 5. Mentorship Participating SMEs will have access to mentorship as part of the programme s broader support ecosystem. Mentorship can provide businesses with practical guidance as they work through trade-related challenges and develop their internationalisation strategies. 6. Business Development The programme also focuses on business development, helping participating SMEs strengthen their commercial readiness and move towards concrete market opportunities. These six pillars collectively form the foundation of the TradeRoots Africa SME support system. How the TradeRoots Africa Programme Works TradeRoots Africa is organised into three progressive tiers . The structure means that participation can develop from foundational trade education to more specialised support and ultimately to export acceleration. Tier 1: Trade Foundations Period: November 2026 – March 2027 The first tier is designed to establish the fundamental knowledge SMEs need before entering regional and international markets. The ICC states that 1,000 SMEs will participate in this stage. Participants will learn about areas including: Export compliance. Trade documentation. AfCFTA. Regional trade fundamentals. Other foundational aspects of exporting. The training will be delivered through a combination of: Virtual and blended webinars. Practical sessions. Capacity-building activities. The programme identifies Modules 1–14 as part of this foundational stage. For SMEs that are still developing their understanding of international trade, this first tier provides an opportunity to strengthen the foundational knowledge required to operate across borders. Tier 2: Digital and Sector Skills Period: April – June 2027 The second tier moves beyond basic trade foundations and focuses on more advanced capabilities. The programme expects 200 SMEs to participate at this stage. Businesses selected for Tier 2 will receive support in areas including: E-commerce. Sustainability-related trade. Trade finance. Market adaptation. Regional and trade-corridor bootcamps. Targeted technical support. Mentorship. Buyer connections. Digital trade readiness. Trade finance readiness workshops. Modules 16–19 are identified for this stage, alongside additional technical and business support activities. This stage is particularly relevant to SMEs that have progressed beyond basic export knowledge and are looking to develop more specialised capabilities for entering or expanding within regional markets. Tier 3: Export Acceleration Period: July–August 2027 The third tier focuses on turning export readiness into practical commercial opportunities. The programme expects 50 SMEs to participate at this stage. Businesses reaching Tier 3 will receive support related to: Developing export plans. Accessing new markets. Securing trade finance. Transaction support. Buyer engagement. Trade finance facilitation. One-to-one sessions. Continued business development. The ICC specifically identifies Module 18 on transaction support as part of this stage. Important Progression Requirement An important point for prospective applicants is that the three tiers are not presented as separate, independent opportunities. The ICC states that only SMEs that participate in Tier 1 are eligible for Tier 2 and Tier 3 . This means that SMEs interested in progressing to the more advanced digital, sector-specific and export acceleration support should understand that participation begins with the foundational stage. Who Is TradeRoots Africa For? TradeRoots Africa is designed for African small and medium-sized enterprises that have potential to scale across African markets. The programme specifically seeks a balanced cohort comprising: Emerging SMEs Growth-stage businesses Established SMEs The common factor is the potential for these businesses to expand and scale across African markets. This means the opportunity is not limited exclusively to newly established businesses. More established SMEs can also be considered where they demonstrate the potential to expand across African markets. TradeRoots Africa and the African Continental Free Trade Area A significant component of the programme is its connection to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) . AfCFTA is referenced by the ICC as one of the key frameworks within which TradeRoots Africa will help SMEs become export-ready. The programme also considers the role of Regional Economic Communities (RECs) , recognising that African businesses can operate within both continental and regional trade frameworks. For SMEs, understanding these frameworks can be important when considering expansion into markets beyond their home country. TradeRoots Africa therefore seeks to make trade policy more practical for businesses by connecting knowledge of continental and regional trade arrangements with practical capabilities such as export compliance, documentation, market access, logistics, digital trade and finance. What Businesses Can Gain From TradeRoots Africa The programme provides several potential areas of development for participating SMEs. Export Readiness One of the central objectives is to help businesses become better prepared for exporting. This includes understanding export compliance and documentation, as well as gaining knowledge of regional trade requirements. Market Access Businesses can develop greater awareness of opportunities to access regional and international markets. Later programme activities also include buyer connections and market adaptation support. Trade Finance Readiness TradeRoots Africa incorporates trade finance into its support framework, including dedicated trade finance readiness workshops and facilitation during the export acceleration stage. Digital Business Capabilities Businesses participating in later stages can develop capabilities relating to digital trade and e-commerce. These skills can be particularly relevant to SMEs seeking to reach customers and commercial partners beyond their traditional geographic markets. Mentorship and Technical Support Participants can benefit from mentorship and targeted technical support as they develop their trade capabilities. Buyer Connections The programme s advanced stages include buyer connections and buyer engagement, creating opportunities for participating businesses to move beyond training towards practical commercial relationships. Export Planning At the export acceleration stage, selected SMEs will work on export plans and receive support related to entering new markets. These components demonstrate that TradeRoots Africa is structured around progression from learning and capacity building towards practical export activity.
